evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction with 50% Barlican in distilled water; challenge concentrations 50%, 25%, 10% in distilled water; readings at day 24 and 25; albino guinea pigs (n=10 experimental, n=5 control).
evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig maximization test (GPMT), albino guinea pigs were induced with 50% Barlican tox-batch and then challenged with various concentrations (50%, 25%, 10%). On challenge day 24, the experimental group (n=10) showed 10/10 positive reactions for erythema and oedema at all challenge concentrations, whereas the control group (n=5) showed 0/5. On challenge day 25, the experimental group again showed 10/10 positive at all concentrations, with some notes of scaliness and eschar, while control showed only 1/5 at 50% erythema. This indicates that Barlican tox-batch is a skin sensitizer.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: 0.5% w/v DCNB in 0.9% aqueous saline with Freund's complete adjuvant; boost: 1.0% w/v DCNB in acetone, occluded 48 h patch; challenge: 0.1% w/v DCNB in acetone, Finn Chambers, 24 h occlusion; scoring at 48 h and 72 h post-application.
evidence.support_text: In both a rigorously conducted guinea pig maximization test and in a modified murine local lymph node assay, DCNB was demonstrated to possess weak sensitizing activity. In the GPMT, test guinea pigs were induced with 0.5% w/v DCNB in saline with Freund's complete adjuvant, boosted with 1.0% w/v DCNB in acetone, and challenged with 0.1% w/v DCNB in acetone. Reactions were scored at 48 h and 72 h, and the results indicated that DCNB induced weak sensitization.

evidence.support_text: Ten guinea pigs were tested in the maximization test with 2% Glyceryl Laurate for sensitizing injections, then challenged with intradermal 0.8% and topical 25% Glyceryl Laurate. evidence.support_text: In the reconstructed human skin model Episkin, 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene (DNCB) was detoxified by glutathione S-transferase forming the glutathione adduct DNP-SG with an apparent Vmax/Km ratio of 1.0 ± 0.2 μL.min^-1.mg prot^-1. evidence.assay_type: In vivo free thiol depletion assay
evidence.experimental_conditions: In vivo mouse model; unsensitized (ICD) or DNCB-sensitized (ACD) mice; topical challenge with 50 µmol of 0.5% DNCB in acetone; skin excised at various time points; free thiol levels determined spectrophotometrically by reaction with DTNB.
evidence.support_text: When mice were challenged with DNCB, cutaneous levels of glutathione and free SH groups rapidly decreased in both the ICD and ACD groups (Fig 1). The decreased glutathione and SH returned to their initial levels more rapidly in mice with ACD than with ICD. Levels of free SH in the ACD group increased further and remained at high levels for at least 7 d. The levels of glutathione and SH remained unaffected in control animals treated concurrently with acetone (data not shown).
